intro: You run a shop and need someone local who understands retail bookkeeping — reconciling tills, tracking stock and keeping on top of VAT. Searching for a retail bookkeeper near me usually means you want a person who can work with your EPOS system and make the numbers add up without a fuss. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK bookkeeper who quotes you directly, so you can compare and choose.
need_heading: What people searching for a retail bookkeeper near me usually need
need_lead: Most shop owners want a bookkeeper who can take the paperwork off their hands and keep the figures straight.
needs: You are spending evenings matching till readings and card payment slips instead of running your shop.
Your stock counts are done but never seem to line up with what the books say, and you want that gap explained.
You are unsure whether your bookkeeper can pull figures straight from your EPOS system to save time.
You need help preparing VAT returns that reflect the seasonal ups and downs of retail cash flow.
You want someone nearby who can visit the shop occasionally and understand how your till and stock systems work.
context_heading: What to understand about retail bookkeeping
context: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

Good bookkeepers are clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice. Ask whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the kind of shop you run and how many till points or card machines you have.
Mention whether you use an EPOS system and whether it can export data for your bookkeeper.
Say how often you do stock counts and whether you need help making them match the accounts.
Explain whether you are VAT registered and how often you need to submit returns.
Note if your sales are seasonal and whether cash flow planning is a priority for you.
Let us know if you already work with an accountant and where you would like the bookkeeper's work to stop.
questions_heading: Questions to ask a retail bookkeeper
questions: Can you work with my EPOS system to pull sales and card payment data directly?
How do you usually reconcile till readings and card payments for a shop like mine?
What is your approach to stock counts and how they feed into the accounts?
Are you supervised by HMRC or a professional body for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's begin for year-end accounts and tax advice?

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper who is local to my shop?
faqs.a: A local bookkeeper can visit your shop to see how your till and stock systems work, which can be helpful for retail. However, many bookkeepers work remotely and can still reconcile EPOS data and prepare VAT returns. It depends on how hands-on you want them to be.

faqs.q: How do bookkeepers handle stock counts for a retail business?
faqs.a: Bookkeepers use stock counts to check that the value of stock in your accounts matches what is actually on the shelves. They may ask you to do regular counts or help you set up a simple system. This keeps your accounts accurate and can highlight shrinkage or ordering issues.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper help with VAT returns for a shop?
faqs.a: Yes, preparing VAT returns is a common part of retail bookkeeping. They will need your sales records, including till and card payment data, and purchase invoices. If you are unsure about VAT rules, ask whether they can explain them or whether you need an accountant.

faqs.q: What should I check before hiring a retail bookkeeper?
faqs.a: Ask which body supervises them for anti-money-laundering purposes, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how they work with EPOS and stock counts. Also clarify where their work ends and an accountant's begins. iComply can introduce you to a bookkeeper who can answer these questions.
